newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady, looks to cash.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady, looks to cash.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Friday after taking a slight hit in the morning following news of an unexpectedly low award by India for June delivery diesel, traders said.
"The market is drifting right now before physical trading starts this evening," one trader said.
May swaps were last quoted at $25.35/$25.45, down from Wednesday's $25.55/$25.65, brokers said.

Traders said the market rebounded slightly from its early morning lows following buying from a few Chinese-related companies and suspicions among some that the recent buying spree by local traders may not be over yet.
Prices had initially come off because the market had on Wednesday expected IOC to buy around 600,000 tonnes compared to the 270,000 tonnes awarded, they said.
Traders said the lower IOC award does not necessarily mean that there would be a surplus of another 300,000 tonnes as most players usually make offers into IOC without having the barrels in hand.
"Traders usually offer short into IOC and will cover the barrels when they win something," one trader said.
The comments were made amid suggestions by some that the market may come under strong selling pressure due to the low IOC award as the surplus barrels would need to be placed elsewhere.
May traded in the morning at $25.25, $25.30 and $25.35 per barrel with about 300,000 barrels exchanging hands, brokers said.
Lower prices were also attributed to an overnight fall to June Brent on the International Petroleum Exchange which closed down 23 cents to $18.29 per barrel.
The market was also uncertain whether or not the buying spree by the local traders has come to an end.

Hin Leong, together with two other traders, have since March 3 bought almost 18 million barrels of physical gas oil, but their purchases so far this week have not been spectacular compared to last week's one-day record of 2.44 milion barrels purchased.

So far this week, the companies have bought between two and three 150,000-barrel cargoes a day and it is this reduced purchases that led to speculations that the companies were winding down their purchases.
Fuel oil swaps were unchanged in quiet trading with May seen at $98.75/$99.50, brokers said.
